meta.description: Compare TiDB and OceanBase for cloud-native HTAP, MySQL compatibility, and real-time analytics. See which distributed SQL database fits your modernization needs.

props.headline: Cloud-Native, Open Distributed SQL
props.subheadline: MySQL-compatible, real-time HTAP, and compute and storage that scale independently. The distributed SQL database for teams modernizing on the cloud.

props.title: Choose the Right Fit for Your Workload

items.title: TiDB: Cloud-Native HTAP
items.description: Built for cloud-native HTAP and real-time analytics, with low-friction MySQL migration. Unifies transactions and analytics in one system.

items.title: OceanBase: Financial-Grade OLTP
items.description: Often chosen for financial-grade, high-concurrency OLTP and Oracle-replacement scenarios.

props.title: TiDB vs OceanBase: Key Differences
props.subtitle: See how TiDB and OceanBase compare across architecture, compatibility, and cloud-native capabilities.

items.title: TiDB: Compute-Storage Separation
items.description: TiDB separates compute (a stateless SQL layer) from storage (TiKV), coordinated by the Placement Driver, with optional TiFlash columnar replicas for analytics. Scale the exact bottleneck—CPU, storage, or analytics—independently.

items.title: OceanBase: Integrated Architecture
items.description: OceanBase uses an integrated, partition-based architecture that couples compute and storage more tightly. Scaling requires coordinated partition rebalancing.

props.title: HTAP & Real-Time Analytics—TiDB's Strength
props.subtitle: TiFlash keeps columnar replicas and the optimizer pushes query fragments to them. One query spans row and column stores on live operational data, with no ETL.

items.title: Native Columnar Store
items.description: TiFlash automatically replicates data in columnar format for fast analytics.

items.title: No ETL Required
items.description: Query live operational data in real time without moving or transforming it.

items.title: Unified Query Engine
items.description: One SQL query seamlessly spans row and column stores for optimal performance.

items.title: Kubernetes Operator
items.description: Native Kubernetes operator and multi-cloud deployment flexibility for seamless orchestration.

items.title: Open Source
items.description: Control your own roadmap, not a vendor's. Contribute, customize, and extend as needed.

items.title: MySQL Protocol & Syntax
items.description: Lower migration friction and tooling reuse with full MySQL compatibility.

props.title: One Engine, Not a Bolt-On Stack
props.subtitle: Most teams stitch four or more systems together long before they hit true scale. TiDB consolidates them onto a single distributed SQL engine—lower cost, fewer failure modes, no ETL, and AI-ready.

items.title: Operational Database

items.title: Analytics Warehouse
items.description: Eliminate Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift with native columnar HTAP via TiFlash—no ETL pipelines.

items.title: Search & Vector Store
items.description: Built-in full-text and vector search replaces Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and standalone vector databases.

items.title: Sharding & Caching
items.description: Transparent auto-sharding with strong consistency—no app-side sharding middleware or external caches.

items.title: Kimi: <1s Database Provisioning per Agent Task
items.description: Runs a production agent-hosting platform on TiDB Cloud with elastic, strongly consistent scale.

items.title: Manus: 2 Weeks to Migrate
items.description: Viral agentic AI platform migrated to TiDB Cloud with no application rewrite.

items.title: Plaud: 10x QPS Under Peak Load
items.description: Eliminated MySQL write-throughput and DDL bottlenecks for 2M+ users across 170 countries.

items.title: Dify: 80% Infrastructure Cost Reduction

items.q: Is TiDB or OceanBase better for HTAP workloads?
items.a: TiDB. TiFlash delivers real-time analytics on live data in one system, with no ETL required. OceanBase typically requires external or separate patterns for analytics.

items.q: Is OceanBase better for Oracle replacement?
items.a: OceanBase is frequently chosen for Oracle-replacement and financial-grade OLTP scenarios. TiDB is MySQL-first—the stronger fit for teams modernizing MySQL, not Oracle.

items.q: Which is easier to operate in Kubernetes?
items.a: TiDB is cloud-native with a mature Kubernetes operator and multi-cloud flexibility, making it easier to deploy and manage in container orchestration environments.

items.q: Are TiDB and OceanBase both MySQL compatible?
items.a: Both offer MySQL compatibility. TiDB emphasizes MySQL-first modernization with lower application-migration friction, full MySQL protocol support, and syntax compatibility.
